rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: ON THE HOSTAGE-TAKING INCIDENT LAST AUGUST 23, 2010
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. SYJUCO
About the view that the Philippine government
must continue professing atonement over the recent
Luneta hostage-taking incident wherein eight
Chinese nationals had been killed, Rep. Syjuco
opined that the government needs to stop selfflagellation
because there was no point in taking
responsibility over an unreasonable act of a hostage
taker.
He maintained that this unfortunate incident
cannot be resolved if the government will sweep
the truth under the so-called carpet of international
relations. It is only when all truths are revealed, he
stated, can both Philippine and Chinese governments
acknowledge their pains and restore their
human dignity. He pointed out that no less than
President Benigno Simeon C. Aquino III had
claimed full responsibility over the hostage-taking
incident, a far cry from the actuations of the Chinese
government which had not been equally
apologetic about similar tragedies affecting Filipino
nationals in China, like the senseless killings
by a deranged Chinese national of the Madrigal
family in Tiananmen Square in 2005.
Rep. Syjuco assured Hong Kong residents that
the Philippine government had heard their demand
for a fair and thorough investigation and also
wanted an impartial probe of the incident. He
added that the government had only acted accordingly
on the hostage-taking incident in order to
protect democracy and disallow terrorism to destroy
lives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2010-09-14

rows.title_full: ON THE INFORMAL SETTLERS IN PARANAQUE CITY
rows.abstract: Rep. Olivarez spoke about the plight of informal settlers numbering ... in his district as well as in other areas, who were living in danger zones. Although he clarified that antisquatting and environment-protection laws should be enforced, he stressed that Congress must devise long-term plans for the relocation and livelihood development of informal settlers and proper disposition of public funds in this regard. He urged government agencies concerned to alleviate the plight of informal settlers in danger zones as was mandated by law in order to ensure a humane life for the less privileged.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT since 2010-09-14
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Tiangco, de Jesus, Ejercito, Marcoleta  and Golez(R). Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G033
rows.title_full: ON PRIORITIZING THE YOUTH
rows.title_short: The Role Of Family In The Protection Of Youth
rows.abstract: Rep. Fatima Aliah Q. Dimaporo spoke of her participation as speaker in the World Youth Conference in Mexico on August 23 to 27, 2010, aimed at prioritizing the youth in policies which will be presented in the Declaration of Youth in the UN Gen. Assembly in September 2010 in New York City. Rep. Dimaporo recommended the inclusion of the youth in the center of development as they are the country´s future generation and partners in national development. She expressed the hope that the government would also promote the family and its role in the protection and integral development of young people.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on YOUTH AND SPORTS DEVELOPMENT since 2010-09-14

rows.author: G024
rows.title_full: PROPOSED FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF HEALTH SERVICE UNITS IN HIS DISTRICT
rows.abstract: Rep. Arnel M. Cerafica spoke on the immediate need for the construction of a hospital in his district to provide access to comprehensive health care services and emergency care that barangay health centers could not provide to his constituents. He informed the Body that the only public hospital in Taguig was located in the 2nd District and was too far.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2010-09-14

rows.title_full: ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF COMPREHENSIVE AGRARIAN REFORM LAW
rows.title_short: Speech Of Lagman On Resignation Of Aquino Officials
rows.abstract: FOCUSED ON THE SPEECH DELIVERED BY MINORITY LEADER EDCEL C. LAGMAN LAST AUGUST 23, 2010 WHEREIN HE ASSAILED THE LEGALITY AND CONSTITUTIONALITY OF THE STOCK DISTRIBUTION OPTION (SDO) BEING IMPLEMENTED IN HACIENDA LUISITA AND THE COMPROMISE AGREEMENT BETWEEN HACIENDA LUISITA, INC. (HLI) AND ITS FARM WORKERS. POINTED OUT THAT CONGRESS ALSO RECOGNIZES OTHER COMPONENTS OF THE CARP SUCH AS LEASEHOLD PRODUCTION, PROFIT SHARING AND LABOR ADMINISTRATION AND THAT THE CARP IS BASED ON LAND DISTRIBUTION AS WELL AS ON OTHER MODES OF AGRARIAN REFORM.  DISAGREED WITH THE LEGAL AND CONSTITUIONAL POSTULATES AND CONCLUSIONS OF REP. LAGMAN ON LAND DISTRIBUTION. CONCLUDED THAT CARP HAS FAILED TO ACHIEVE ITS MAIN GOALS. URGED THE GOVERNMENT IN IMPLEMENTING THE CARP BECAUSE THE PROGRAM IS CONCERNED NOT ONLY WITH LAND DISTRIBUTION BUT WITH INCREASED AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTIVITY AS WELL, LEADING TO INDUSTRIALIZATION AND FULL EMPLOYMENT.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRARIAN REFORM since 2010-09-14
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Apostol. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: D068
rows.title_full: ON THE INSPIRING SUCCESS OF MS. VENUS RAJ IN THE 2010 MISS UNIVERSE PAGEANT
rows.abstract: SPOKE ON THE HUMBLE BEGINNINGS, PERSONAL STRUGGLE AND ULTIMATE VICTORY OF MISS UNIVERSE 2010 FOURTH RUNNER-UP MARIA VENUS RAJ WHO HAILS FROM BICOL. SAID THAT FILIPINOS COULD DRAW INSPIRATION AND STRENGTH FROM HER LIFE STORY WHEN CONFRONTED WITH THE HARSH AND PAINFUL REALITIES OF LIFE. EXPRESSED HOPE THAT HER LIFE STORY WOULD SERVE AS A BEACON OF INSPIRATION FOR MANY OF THE YOUTH IN THE CURRENT ENVIRONMENT OF CYNICISM, SKEPTICISM AND UTTER DESPAIR PERVADING IN THE COUNTRY'S SOCIAL AND POLITICAL MILIEU.
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2010-09-14

rows.author: G052
rows.title_full: ON THE CONTROVERSIES AND ISSUES REGARDING THE MWSS
rows.abstract:
Rep. Herrera-Dy exhorted her colleagues to join
her in ferreting out the truth about the serious water shortage which plagued Metro Manila for several months. She initially informed the Body of the legal and regulatory framework of the MWSS and its functions and operations in relation to its concessionaires - the Manila Water Company Incorporated (MWCI) and MAYNILAD- under their concession agreements. Rep. Herrera-Dy expressed concern over the exorbitant water rates, dismal state of sewerage and water
sanitation, lack of comprehensive plan to develop
new water sources and thus provide uninterrupted
and adequate water supply, and unsettled retirement benefits of the MWSS employees. She likewise cited overpriced projects and loan agreements entered into by the agency that have not been completed. She pointed out the causes of exorbitant water rates, and asked whether the consumers are getting their money´s worth.
Finally, she recommended  several plan of actions...
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2010-09-07)

rows.author: A088
rows.title_full: ON THE ALLEGED ANOMALOUS ACTS COMMITTED BY THE NATIONAL COUNCIL FOR INDIGENOUS PEOPLE'S IN ISSUING CERTIFICATE OF ANCESTRAL LAND TITLES IN BAGUIO CITY
rows.abstract: ASKED CONGRESS TO STOP THE UNSCRUPULOUS AND ANOMALOUS ISSUANCE BY THE NATIONAL COMMISSION ON INDIGENOUS PEOPLES (NCIP) OF CERTIFICATES OF ANCESTRAL LAND TITLE (CALTs)COVERING FOREST/WATERSHED AND OTHER GOVERNMENT RESERVATIONS IN BAGUIO CITY. URGED CONGRESS TO PASS MEASURES TO DELIMIT THE NCIP's POWERS AND INSURE THAT IT WOULD NOT AWARD CALTs NOR ENTERTAIN CALT APPLICATIONS COVERING THE BAGUIO CITY GOV'T RESERVATIONS AND LANDS WITHIN THE BAGUIO TOWNSITE RESERVATION... REQUESTED FOR A CONGRESSIONAL INVESTIGATION ON THE MATTER.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL CULTURAL COMMUNITIES since 2010-09-14
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee. Manifestations of Reps. Escudero and Biazon.

rows.author: E041
rows.abstract: POINTED OUT THAT PRES. AQUINO WAS NOWHERE TO BE FOUND WHEN HE WAS BADLY NEEDED TO BE IN CONTROL AND TO EXERCISE HIS LEADERSHIP  IN ORDER TO SAVE THE FOREIGNERS INVOLVED IN THE RECENT HOSTAGE-TAKING CRISIS IN MANILA. WARNED THE PRESIDENT THAT THE COUNTRY NEEDS A COMPETENT AND DECISIVE LEADER TO REDEEM NATIONAL HONOR AND EXCULPATE ITS CITIZENRY FROM ECONOMIC AND POLITICAL BANKRUPTCY. STRESSED THAT THE FIRST ACID TEST OF PRES. AQUINO'S LEADERSHIP IS CHOOSING THE RIGHT PEOPLE FOR HIS CABINET AND ASKED HOW MANY MORE CABINET OFFICIALS HAVE NOT SHOWN COMPETENCE. STRESSED THAT HER SPEECH WAS INTENDED TO GIVE CONSTRUCTIVE CRITICISMS IN THE HOPE THAT HE WILL DELIVER TO THE PEOPLE HIS CAMPAIGN PROMISE OF GIVING WISE AND COMPETENT LEADERSHIP. EXPRESSED HOPE THAT HE WILL PUNISH THE CULPRITS IF ONLY TO REGAIN THE COUNTRY'S HONOR AND RESPECT.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2010-09-08)
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Rep. Biazon, Golez(R)and Bag-ao.

rows.author: F123
rows.title_full: PROPOSED PRIVATIZATION OF NAPOCOR'S AGUS-PULANGI HYDRO COMPLEX IN MINDANAO
rows.abstract:
Rep. Mendoza (R.) expressed the outrage and
disappointment of the people of Mindanao over the
privatization of the crown jewel of the Napocor - the Agus-Pulangui Hydropower Complex - which provided the region with cheap electricity and majority of its power needs. He said that the Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA) in 2001 failed to address energy monopolies, low electricity rates, and power shortages. He explained that the Power Sector Assets and Liabilities Management Corporation (PSALM)
must not sell the complex to a private company
because it would affect workers, increase power
tariffs, result in monopolies and price manipulation, widen income disparities, and fuel existing social conflict. Stressing that the government must use natural resources for the common good, he asked the Members to investigate the matter and join the crusade to protect the interest of the Filipinos in general and the Mindanaoans in particular.
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2010-11-30
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Evardone, Fua, Marcoleta. Referred to the appropriate committee. Considered as substituted by H.R. No. 823 - URGING PSALM TO DEFER THE SALE AND PRIVATIZATION OF THE AGUS AND PULANGUI HYDROELECTRIC PLANT COMPLEXES IN MINDANAO

committee_action.action: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2010-11-30

rows.author: B006
rows.title_full: US PASTOR TERRY JONES' PLAN TO HOST AN \"INTERNATIONAL BURN A QU'RAN DAY
rows.title_short: Plan To Burn Quran By A Pastor
rows.abstract:
Although American Pastor Terry Jones had put
on hold his plan to host an “International Burn-a-Qur´an Day” on the ninth anniversary of the
September 11, 2001 terrorist attack of the United
States after it drew international condemnation,
Rep. Balindong said, he had already ignited a wave of resentment and rage in the Muslim world. He stressed that the Qur´an is the eternal and literal word of God and a venerated and important element of the Muslim faith. He pointed out that throughout history, Muslims have become a spectacle to ridicule or to fear because of ignorance, prejudice, and paranoia.
In ending his speech, Rep. Balindong condemned
terrorism but expressed the Muslims´ prayer for genuine, honorable, and lasting peace anchored
on justice and sincerity.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on MUSLIM AFFAIRS since 2010-09-21

rows.author: F034
rows.title_full: LEGISLATORS AS ACTIVE CONTRIBUTORS TO THE BUDGET PREPARATION PROCESS
rows.abstract:
Rep. Aurelio “Dong” D. Gonzales Jr. spoke about the active and vital role played by Members of Congress in the regional development councils (RDCs), which had a positive impact on the budget preparation process. He recalled that the late Pres. Corazon C. Aquino issued a series of EOs providing for the inclusion of the Representatives and Senators in the membership of the regional consultative assemblies (RCAs) which were created as deliberative and consultative bodies to advise and cooperate with the RDCs in discharging their functions. He pointed out that former Pres. Fidel V. Ramos repealed these issuances and came up with EO No. 325 wherein the Members of the House, will now be part of a regional development advisory committee whose membership is voluntary
and the intention to join must be in writing. He
then urged Pres. Benigno Simeon C. Aquino III
to reinstate the mandatory membership of Members
of Congress in the RDCs to aid in the speedy and
effective approval of the national budget.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2010-09-21

rows.author: E059
rows.title_full: MILLENIUM DEVELOPMENT GOALS - PARTICIPATORY BUDGET
rows.abstract:
Rep. Tañada spoke on the coming Millennium
Development Goals (MDG) +10 Review Summit...
aims to identify challenges, opportunities
and lessons learned and to propose concrete
strategies towards the attainment of all the MDGs
by 2015. He pointed out however that achieving the
central goal...to reduce extreme poverty by 50% has proven to be a deep pothole as poverty incidence in the country went up from 30% in 2003 to 33% in 2006 along with the increase in population. Due to misgovernance and lack of political will, he stressed that the country failed to capitalize on Goal 8 ...which is developing global partnership for development, ...Rep. Tañada said that he filed anew HB No. 219 or the People´s Participation in the Budget Process Bill,...and thus provide citizen monitoring, transparency and accountability, which are the pillars of good governance. Rep. Tañada next expounded on Goal 8 of the MDGs to develop global partnership in the areas of trade, debt and aid for development. He invited the
Members to support the MDGs through the Stand
Up, Take Action Campaign´s MDG Week activities
in Congress, in partnership with the UNDP, the
PLCPD, Social Watch, CODE NGO and the Freedom
from Debt Coalition, with the goals of fighting
extreme poverty and achieving the MDGs through
participatory processes and responsive legislations. He concluded that this is an auspicious time for social change under the present Administration of popular mandate and mindset for reform.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2010-09-21
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Biazon, Bello and Lagman. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: E063
rows.title_short: Actions Of C O M E L E C And D I L G In Compostela, Cebu
rows.abstract:
Since July 2010, Rep. Durano said that none of
the duly proclaimed mayor, vice mayor and councilors of Compostela, Cebu have performed their functions and that the town has been supervised by a caretaker designated by the DILG-Region 7. He asked the House to immediately stop the anomalous and undemocratic situation caused by unjust and reckless acts of the Comelec
in general and Comm. Nicodemus Ferrer in particular. Rep. Durano then described the sad state of Compostela´s economic and peace and order situation as a result of the appointment of a caretaker local chief executive. He also disclosed how the Comelec has not acted upon the Mayor Quiño´s petition for the Comelec en banc to overturn the Ferrer resolution as well as on his motion for summary dismissal. Rep. Durano called on the Committee on Good Government and Public Accountability to investigate the inaction and highly irregular actions of the Comelec and the DILG and for the House to file the proper charges against the culprits and to initiate impeachment proceedings against the impeachable officials.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2010-09-13)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Biazon. Referred to the Committee on Good Government.

rows.author: G085
rows.abstract:
Rep. Sarmiento discussed the innovative, ecologically friendly fishing methods espoused by the Food and Agriculture Organization and which are being tested by the proper government agencies in domestic waters to help ensure food security and protect biodiversity. He then
showed a ppt presentation of data supporting
his cause and a short video produced by the
British Broadcasting Corp. about fishing for
sustainable development. Rep. Sarmiento (M.) stressed that to be genuinely sustainable, effective legislation and policies must be put in place to continue to harness the benefits
of the environment and at the same time manage
the possible harmful human impacts. He then
recommended the ff: 1) revisit RA No.8550 - Fisheries Code ... to intensify the implementation and enforcement of its policies; 2) come up with incentives for fisherfolks who will be using Juvenile and Trash Excluder Devices or any other device that is proven to be environmentally friendly; 3) encourage and intensify research and development among the concerned government agencies, academe, NGOs, private organizations and mass media for information dissemination; and 4) enhance effort control system including closed seasons during spawning months. He then encouraged the Members to
view with optimism, stand up and take action on
the remaining five years before the MDG deadline.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2010-09-13)

rows.author: G078
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR THE INVESTIGATION ON THE ABANDONED NEWBORN BABY BOY ON A GULF AIR FLIGHT FROM BAHRAIN
rows.title_short: The Case Of Baby George Francis
rows.abstract:
Rep. Mercado-Revilla called for an inquiry on the case of the newborn baby boy found in the toilet trash bin of a Gulf Air plane which arrived recently in Manila from Bahrain. She related the details of the baby´s discovery and the efforts to locate the mother who abandoned the boy. She also cited certain provisions of pertinent laws which stress the importance of promoting the best interest of the child, penalize the crime of abandonment, and mandate the State to assist a parent for the proper care and maintenance of his or her family. Rep. Mercado-Revilla expressed her sympathies...to the mother of the baby boy who was named George Francis. She called it hypocrisy for the government to praise the OFWs) as modern-day heroes and yet, does nothing to help them when they are in trouble. She also criticized those who utter bad innuendoes
on the circumstances which caused the mother...
to abandon the baby boy. She then urged the people and the government to extend assistance to the woman and to help her find the right path even as Rep. Mercado-Revilla clarified that she does not condone the woman´s actions. She then addressed the mother to show herself up and if necessary, to call on the lawmaker for any personal or official assistance she might need in dealing with government authorities. Rep. Mercado-Revilla opined that as an OFW, the woman deserves the understanding and care of her countrymen, and not their undue judgment, as she goes through a personal battle.
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2010-12-14

Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2010-12-14

rows.author: G057
rows.title_full: REPRESENTATION OF MUSLIM FILIPINOS IN THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT UNDER RA 9054 (STRENGTHENING AND EXPANDING THE ORGANIC ACT FOR ARMM)
rows.abstract:
Rep. Loong took the floor to urge Pres. Benigno Simeon C. Aquino III to respect and comply with the mandate of RA 9054, granting the representation of Muslim Filipinos in the central government to show the sincerity of his
administration in bringing about just and lasting
peace in Mindanao. Specifically, he questioned the recommendation made by Presidential Adviser on the Peace Process Teresita “Ging” Deles of Dr.
Hamid Barra to chair the newly created National
Commission on Muslim Filipinos and sit as a member of the government peace panel, which was done without due consultations with the legitimate leaders of the Muslim Filipinos.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on MUSLIM AFFAIRS since 2010-09-21

rows.author: C045
rows.title_short: Judges Mass Leave And Impeachment Case Against Ombudsman Gutierrez
rows.abstract:
Rep. Fariñas rose on two concerns: 1) on the
judges´ pronouncement to go on mass leave of absence because of low salaries and benefits. He disclosed that the law provides that government workers cannot go on mass leave of absence or on concerted effort to paralyze the government and that he challenged them to resign if they believe that they are underpaid; and 2) on the order of the Supreme Court to the House Committee on Justice to respond to a petition
filed by Ma. Merceditas N. Gutierrez who is a
respondent to the impeachment case filed by the said Committee, and to observe the status quo. He disagreed with the Supreme Court decision and cited pertinent arguments and cases in support of his position. Rep. Fariñas then appealed to the Supreme Court justices to exercise judicial statesmanship and restraint and at the same time, allow the House of Representatives,
in the exercise of its own Rules, to oversee
the actions of the Committee on Justice. He also
recommended that the House leadership call for an
all-Member caucus to take a position regarding the Supreme Court´s decision and possibly, defend the House of Representatives against the attack by a coequal branch of government.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2010-09-15
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Escudero, Bello, Lagman, Marcoleta, Rodriguez (R.) and Gullas. Referred to the Cttee. on Justice.

rows.author: A040
rows.title_full: STATE OF THE INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS INDUSTRY
rows.abstract:
Rep. Golez´ speech re: the rapid development
of the Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) and
the Information, Communications and Technology
(ICT) sectors in the country initially underscored the amount of investments and revenues therein, including the statistics on the increase in employment and the extent of subscribers´ base and location of expansion
of the ICT and BPO industries; claimed that
the rapid expansion of the two industries ...in the country could dictate the course of new politics in the country and worldwide; maintained that in the global BPO market alone, the Philippines placed third with a market share of 15% of the world´s BPO market. Rep. Golez further talked about the speed of technology and how it was being used by just anyone and everyone, and how it could surpass even the human brain in the years to come; speculated on whether the government has an agenda in the ICT as he stressed its effect on good governance, people empowerment and better delivery of services.
rows.status: Scheduled for first meeting/hearing on 2011-05-16
rows.remarks: Interpellation of Rep. Biazon.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

committee_action.action: Scheduled for first meeting/hearing on 2011-05-16
committee_action.meethigh: The Committee instructed the Commission on Information and Communications Technology, Department of National Defense, Department of Science and Technology, National Telecommunications Commission, National Computer Center, Departments of Education, Environment and Natural Resources and Justice to meet and clarify the direction of the national broadband project in the country and submit a report to the Committee within thirty (30) days.

rows.author: G012
rows.title_full: CONDEMNED THE KILLING OF POLICEMEN COMMITTED BY THE NEW PEOPLE'S ARMY IN CATARMAN, NORTHERN SAMAR
rows.abstract:
Rep. Leopoldo N. Bataoil called for the immediate resumption of the peace talks with the Communist rebels and for a review of the government´s campaign to end insurgency; also condemned what he called the atrocities
and barbaric acts of members of the New People´s
Army (NPA)...; claimed that more NPA atrocities had resulted in the deaths of military, police and civilians due to the apparent complacency of the new Administration; called on the national government to resume transparent and participative peace negotiations with the Communist rebels and to seriously pursue peace by addressing the root causes of insurgency; condemned the use of landmines in the Northern Samar ambush and expressed his support for the members of the police and military who were always ready to serve and protect the people and to sacrifice their lives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2010-09-28
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Biazon. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G105
rows.abstract:
Rep. Emerenciana “Emmi” A. De Jesus spoke to put an end to the government´s housing programs
for urban poor that enable private real estate
corporations and businessmen to amass huge gains at the expense of the poor; pointed out that said housing programs did not comply with the real needs of the urban poor dwellers such as water, electricity, sanitation, schools
and hospitals but purely served business
opportunities with the help of government agencies; cited interviews and data regarding the
plight of the relocatees in the different relocation sites and enumerated their appeal for the 1) inclusion HRs No. 208, 341 and 342 in the legislative priority; 2) a moratorium on housing demolition until after the formulation of a humane housing program; 3) an investigation on the status of government housing programs in different relocation sites and on the alleged collusion between the National Housing Authority and private real estate corporations; emphasized
the need to resolve the issue of homelessness in
the country.
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2011-05-25

committee_action.action: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2011-05-25

rows.title_full: ROLE OF THE OMBUDSMAN IN THE AUGUST 23, 2010 HOSTAGE-TAKING FIASCO
rows.abstract:
Rep. Garcia spoke on the duty of Congress to see
to it that the laws it passed are implemented correctly and properly; referred to the August 23, 2010 hostage-taking incident in Luneta which was triggered by Sr.Inspector Rolando Mendoza's dismissal from police service with forfeiture of benefits as ordered by the Ofc. of the Ombudsman;
explained why the Office of the Ombudsman does not have any jurisdiction or authority
to take cognizance of the administrative case filed against Mendoza and also to order the latter´s dismissal from the PNP; cited Sec.13, Art.XII of the 1987 Constitution, pertinent provisions of RA No.6770 or the Ombudsman Law and RA No. 6975 or the PNP Law, to substantiate his position; surmised that if only some government functionaries did not succumb to the natural but irrational tendency to just take many things and practices for granted so as not to disturb the status quo, the Office
of the Ombudsman would not have issued a decision
on a case that legally never was, and that dreadful human tragedy at the Luneta would not have happened.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2010-09-28

rows.author: A010
rows.title_full: CONSTITUTIONAL CRISIS BETWEEN THE HOUSE AND THE SUPREME COURT RE: STATUS QUO ANTE ORDER OF THE SUPREME COURT ON THE PROCEEDINGS OF THE IMPEACHMENT CASE AGAIINST OMBUDSMAN GUTIERREZ
rows.abstract:
Rep. Erico B. Aumentado spoke on two controversial issues concerning the Judiciary: First: expounded on the Supreme Court´s status quo ante order on the impeachhment case against Ombudsman Merceditas Gutierrez which, he surmised, could lead to a major constitutional crisis on the argument that the House of Representatives has the constitutional prerogative to initiate and investigate impeachment complaints and the right to defend its jurisdiction and authority. Second: discussed the threat of judges and court personnel to go on mass leave because of the decision of the Executive Department to cut by half the Judiciary´s proposed budget in 2011.
Rep. Aumentado urged the High Tribunal to resolve
the Ombudsman´s case at the soonest possible
time to allow the House Committee on Justice to perform its constitutional mandate; also agreed on the proposal to discuss the judicial budgetary cuts through the convening of the Judicial-Executive-Legislative Advisory and Consultative Council (JELACC); enjoined the contending parties involved in these issues from the Judiciary, the Executive and the Legislative departments, to exercise statesmanship and to observe the rule of law.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2010-09-28
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Rep. Apostol and Fua. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.manual_status: Committee Report No. 01988, recommending adoption of HR No. 1035
rows.author: F100
rows.title_full: THE ILLEGAL ARREST AND DETENTION, AND THE EXTREME TORTURE EXPERIENCED BY THEN HUMAN RIGHTS ACTIVIST, NERI COLMENARES IN SEPTEMBER 23, 1972 (VIOLATIONS OF THE ANTI-TORTURE LAW AND HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS COMMITTED DURING THE MARTIAL LAW PERIOD)
rows.abstract:
Rep. Colmenares spoke about the apparent disregard for the Anti-Torture Law...Related his
experiences as a torture victim during martial law days when he was an activist in his teenage years.  Said that he continued to be incarcerated despite his acquittal and the dismissal of his cases because the arrest order against him had not been withdrawn. Rep. Colmenares rued the fact that 1) the
billion-dollar compensation which the Hawaii court awarded to the human rights victims had been thwarted by the Marcoses and the Philippine government; 2) the victims´ lawyer attempted to settle with the Marcoses for a lesser amount through an agreement that even stated that Pres. Marcos had not committed any wrongdoing during martial law; 3) the Compensation Bill had not yet been passed; 4) billions of pesos turned over by Swiss banks could not be clearly accounted for; and 5) most of the awardees had grown old and some had already died. Emphasized that despite the end of martial law and the passage of the Anti-Torture Law, torture and military power persisted and the struggle for the protection of human rights continued. Urged the Members to ensure justice for martial law victims and to remind the people of the atrocities committed in one of the most
brutal and bloody chapters in Philippine history so that they would continue to resist the return of martial law.
rows.status: Committee Report on Adopted Measure Pending with Rules since 2012-03-07

second_reading.comm_report_action: Recommending the adoption of House Resolution No. 1035

rows.author: E041
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR THE RESUMPTION OF THE IMPEACHMENT CASE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST OMBUDSMAN GUTIERREZ
rows.abstract:
Rep. Magsaysay (M.) said she wanted to protect
the House from being encroached upon, disrespected, and marginalized by the Supreme Court under the guise of exercising its judicial review power in the impeachment case against Ombudsman Merceditas Gutierrez; appealed to her colleagues to protect their mandate and proceed with said case; pointed out that the SC has once again encroached on the prerogatives and powers of the House on the impeachment process; noted that the status quo ante order is premature, illegal and is suspect of being more political than legal as shown by the voting result wherein Chief Justice Corona and those identified with him voted in favor of Ombudsman Gutierrez; stressed that the Members should not allow the SC to dictate upon the House as the former does not have jurisdiction over impeachment cases and that the power of judicial review, although provided under the 1987 Constitution, has limitation as it involves a coequal branch of government; pointed out that the House has not deprived Ombudsman Gutierrez of her right to due process as the Ctte. on Justice is still holding hearings and that she can still be heard and present her side. Stressing that they should not heed the status quo ante order, Rep. Magsaysay enjoined the Members to make a bipartisan stand on the matter, defend the mandate of the House as an independent institution and not to allow another coequal branch of government to interfere with their work.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2010-09-28
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Rep. Fuentebella. Referred to the Committee on Justice.

rows.author: G067
rows.title_full: STATE OF RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Rep. Angelo B. Palmones spoke on the need
for the leaders and policy planners of the country to recognize the benefits derived from advances in science and technology and to develop strategies to harness the explosion in new knowledge made possible by research and development (R&D); described in detail the general state of R&D in the Philippines,
particularly on the following areas of concern: insufficient R&D funds provided to the science community; inadequate number of trained R&D personnel; inadequate infrastructure for R&D; need for better R&D and extension program coordination; outdated financial management for R&D; and high taxes on the importation of research tools and equipment; cited the accomplishments of the country´s
researchers and engineers in various fields;
recommended measures to help the country´s fledgling science and technology sector
and to harness the potentials of research and development to help the poor; emphasized that the
country´s ability to address its basic problems and sustain its economic growth greatly depends on science, technology and innovation in economic transformation in particular, and sustainable development in general.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY since 2010-09-28
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep.Golez. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G103
rows.title_full: ROLE OF PARLIAMENTARIANS OF THE PLCPD TO ACHIEVE THE MILLENNIUM DEVELOPMENT GOALS
rows.abstract:
In line with the Tenth Anniversary of the Philippines´ MDGs launched in Congress during the past week, Rep. Obillo shared her experience as a participant in the Regional Consultation on “Emerging Economies and Population: Reproductive Health Programmes” held
recently in Bangkok, Thailand; said that the MDGs is an international agreement of UN-member States, inc. the Philippines, to reduce poverty and the worst forms of human deprivation through collaborative action aimed at accomplishing eight goals with specific targets by 2015; averred that the conference focused on MDGs 4, 5 and 6 which are health-related targets
concerning reduction of child mortality, improvement of maternal health, and the combat of
HIV/AIDS, malaria, tuberculosis and other diseases, respectively. ... Rep. Obillo opined that it is crucial to act collectively to ensure positive results through pertinent legislation, information and education campaigns, and monitoring and feedback mechanisms.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2010-09-28

rows.author: G087
rows.title_full: UNCERTAIN FUTURE OF OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS
rows.abstract:
Rep. Singson talked about the positive economic
contributions of the OFWs, their reasons for working abroad despite the attendant risks and social repercussions, and the uncertain
future that awaits the OFWs based in the
United States and certain European countries which had decided to impose an imminent clampdown on the employment of OFWs to put preference in the employment of their respective countrymen. As these would pose grave repercussions to the national economy, he expressed hope that the administration of Pres. Benigno Simeon C. Aquino III would soon take the necessary steps to generate more employment opportunities in the country to make the OFWs want to stay rather than work abroad.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2010-09-28

rows.author: G078
rows.title_full: COASTAL WATERS CLEAN - UP DAY
rows.abstract: Rep. Mercado-Revilla invited all the Members to participate in the forthcoming 25th Annual Internat'l Coastal Clean-Up Day... an annual event observed in many countries throughout the world; mentioned the different clean-up programs implemented in her province which all seek to promote environmental protection; appealed to the DENR for the rehabilitation and development of Bacoor Bay and other bays in the country;... underscored that what is wanting is the effective implementation of the laws at both national and local levels; concluded that the Members are duty bound to preserve and protect all other nature for the sake of both the present and future generations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2010-09-28
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Rep. Pacquiao. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G007
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR THE CONVENING OF THE LEDAC TO IDENTIFY AND PREPARE THE MEDIUM - TERM DEVELOPMENT PLAN
rows.title_short: L E D A C / Medium - Term Philippine Development Plan
rows.abstract:
... Rep. Apacible urged the House to start
convening the Legislative-Executive Dev't
Advisory Council (LEDAC) in order to discuss the
formulation of the 2011-2016 Medium-Term Philippine Development Plan (MTPDP); opined that
the NEDA, the DBM, and Congress should strengthen the planning and budgeting processes through closer collaboration and that they should already start formulating the MTPDP by organizing the working committees on work plans and reporting systems; enumerated the LEDAC´s functions and priorities and then cited the view of civil society that the current MTPDP had failed to address inequality and poverty and to promote a sustainable economy, people empowerment and democratization and that the
general framework of the 2011-2016 MTPDP should
be based on good governance and people empowerment; asked for the speedy approval of
HR No. 400 calling for the convening of the LEDAC, called on the leadership to designate
members thereto pursuant to Sec. 2 of RA No. 7640, and looked forward to the designation
of the head of the Presidential-Legislative Liaison Office (PLLO) to be based in the House of Representatives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECONOMIC AFFAIRS since 2010-09-28
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Loong and Rodriguez R. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G095
rows.title_full: Separation of powers of the Legislature and Judiciary in the light of the Supreme Court status quo ante order on the impeachment case against Ombudsman Gutierrez
rows.title_short: Intervention Of Supreme Court On The Impeachment Proceedings
rows.abstract:
Rep. Umali rose to defend the doctrine of separation of powers and the principle of checks and balances and to invoke the exclusive constitutional mandate of Congress over impeachment cases so as to preclude a probable constitutional crisis; presented several arguments indicating how the Supreme Court overstepped said congressional prerogative and
extended the limits of judicial power esp. when it issued a status quo ante order on the impeachment proceedings ... against Ombudsman Merceditas N. Gutierrez; opined that SC spokesperson and Court Administrator Midas Marquez´ warning of a possible contempt should the House fail to heed a status quo ante order is the height of judicial arrogance, and expressed fear of judicial despotism in reaction to the latter´s statement that the 60-day period which the Constitution mandates the Ctte. on Justice to submit its resolution is suspended because of said order; said that there is no real guarantee that the SC will promptly decide on the petition of the Ombudsman; urged the Members to support his HR No.458, and if necessary, to act thereon as a Committee of the Whole; asked the Ctte. to continue with the proceedings despite the SCs status quo ante order, if only to assert Congress´ independence and position that impeachment is its exclusive prerogative.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2010-11-09
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Biazon, Rodriguez R., Apostol, Cagas, and Garcia P. Manifestation of Rep. Aggabao. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: A088
rows.title_full: Jueteng Controversy in Baguio City
rows.abstract:
Rep. Vergara´s speech initially dealt on the allegation of Archbishop Oscar Cruz,...Senate hearing on the jueteng controversy, that Baguio City Mayor Mauricio G. Domogan is involved
in illegal gambling; underscored that the
Archbishop´s allegations had consequently affected the integrity and honor of the City of Baguio and that of its government officials; however claimed that in a public statement, Mayor Domogan had vehemently denied Archbishop Cruz´s allegation and even ordered the conduct of an investigation of his alleged involvement in illegal gambling and jueteng operations.
Rep. Vergara defended Mayor Domogan considering
the latter´s consistent stand against anti-gambling operations, including jueteng; added that he feels morally compelled to rise in
defense of any public official who may be unduly affected by malicious imputations of wrongdoing, and advised the House to be extra cautious in conducting any future congressional inquiry in aid of legislation on the matter.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY since 2010-11-09

rows.author: G052
rows.title_full: Pending increase in water rates in Metro Manila
rows.abstract:
Rep. Herrera-Dy talked about the issue of the pending increase in water rates in Metro Manila to account for the foreign currency exchange adjustments. ... requested the MWSS to suspend its approval pending an investigation by Congress of alleged anomalies that involve the MWSS and its concessionaires. She also argued that any proposal for an increase in water rates is unjustified considering that one concessionaire, the Maynilad, had claimed that the extension of its concession agreement with the MWSS until 2037 would result to a 75% decrease in tariff rates and consequently, to lower water rates. Rep. Herrera-Dy thereafter urged the MWSS to compute first the amount that should be refunded to consumers on account of an unimplemented project which is the subject of an ongoing legislative inquiry and to determine if there is still a need to charge higher rates before implementing the new rates; and sought for an immediate legislative inquiry on the proposed increase in water rates
before its implementation by the MWSS.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2010-11-09

rows.author: G090
rows.title_full: Alleged jueteng operations in Navotas City
rows.abstract:
Rep. Reynald M. Tiangco delved on the privilege speech of Sen. Miriam Defensor Santiago re: illegal gambling and the inclusion of the cities of Navotas and Malabon in jueteng operations. He
claimed that he has to make several clarifications to protect the reputation and integrity of the citizens of Navotas, to defend his unblemished reputation and integrity as its incumbent Representative and its former mayor, and to defend also the reputation and integrity of his brother, the incumbent mayor, John Reynald M.Tiangco.In his clarification, Rep. Tiangco underscored his claim that even at the start of his term as mayor of Navotas, he had already exhausted all means to eradicate jueteng thereat. Thus, considering all his efforts against illegal gambling ... he does not see any reason why Navotas would be included in Sen. Santiago´s speech as one of the cities raking in revenues from jueteng.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY since 2010-11-09

rows.author: F123
rows.title_full: Welfare of OFWs and creating opportunities for all Filipinos to end the Filipino diaspora
rows.title_short: Overseas Filipino Workers - Romelyn Erog - Ibanez
rows.abstract:
Rep. Mendoza spoke on the death of his son´s
former nanny, Romelyn Eroy Ibañez, an OFW in Saudi Arabia who was found murdered in her employer´s house. He enumerated the positive economic contributions of OFWs and likewise mentioned the bad fate of OFWs who were illegally recruited and eventually become the subjects of abuse, exploitation and cold-blooded killings as in the case of Romelyn. He then proposed several recommendations... that: 1) an inquiry into Romelyn´s cold-blooded murder; 2) for Labor Secretary Rosalinda Baldoz to form an independent team to look into the rules and regulations of the POEA; 3) for the Members put up a united front against any move to slash the budget of the DFA; and 4) the
government to conduct an in-depth evaluation of the country´s labor situation so it can create and offer decent job opportunities for all Filipinos. Called on the DFA and OWWA to assist
Romelyn´s family so that her remains will be
repatriated as soon as possible and that proper
charges be brought against her killer as well as the agency that deployed her.
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2011-02-23

committee_action.action: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2011-02-23

rows.author: F102
rows.title_full: Poverty alleviation policies of the Aquino administration
rows.title_short: Anti - Poverty Policy / Medium-term Development Goals
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bello talked about the speech of Pres. Benigno Simeon C. Aquino III at the UN General Assembly in New York on the challenges confronting developing countries in their efforts to eliminate poverty and meet their
MDGs; Said that Pres. Aquino´s message about the Philippines´ intent on meeting its MDGs, it has been diluted by the appointment of Rep. Imelda R. Marcos as chairperson of the Special Ctte.on MDGs; Suggested that ... based on the President's central pillars of good governance and anti-corruption, Pres. Aquino should accept
the resignation of DILG Undersecretary Rico E. Puno to show that all the President´s men are above suspicion when it comes to corruption; Also urged the Truth Commission to fast track its efforts and for the House Ctte. on Justice to continue with the impeachment of the Ombudsman; Pointed out that the government must
address the four key realities that the last four
post-EDSA administrations have failed to seriously confront, to wit: 1) curb the runaway population growth; 2) do something drastic about the country´s debt servicing burden; 3) reverse the trade liberalization that has devastated the Phil.industry and turned the country into a net food importer instead of being a net food exporter; & 4) implement a genuine land reform;
Urged to approve the RH Bill, repeal
the Automatic Appropriations Act and review
the impact of intern'l trade agreements that
the country has entered into, and for Pres.
Aquino to resolve the Hacienda Luisita agrarian
case.
rows.status: Referred to stakeholders on 2010-12-07
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Rep.Garin(J.) and Escudero. Referred to the appropriate committee.

committee_action.action: Referred to stakeholders on 2010-12-07

rows.author: G085
rows.title_full: Alternative to Clean Water Act
rows.abstract:
Rep.Sarmiento spoke on the reason why the quality of Philippine waters, esp. in densely populated areas and regions of industrial and agricultural activities have been polluted and also cited its adverse effects; ... lamented that despite the passage of RA 9275 or the Clean Water Act of 2004, not much progress has been done to solve water pollution; ... noted that 94% of highly urbanized cities are not connected to a sewerage system and this shows the need for the government to increase its investment...to build physical infrastructures for sanitation and sewerage; claimed that LGUs are also beset
with the same problems and thus need considerable
investments to address water quality problems
and sewerage systems; ... stressed that
the lack of resources need not be a reason for seeking development of improved sewerage and sanitation facilities; cited available alternatives for costly centralized sewerage system...; maintained that the use of local and indigenous products for wastewater treatment is less expensive and in accordance with the provisions of the Clean Water Act of 2004.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2010-11-09

rows.author: F099
rows.title_full: Electric/water services cooperatives
rows.title_short: Electric Cooperatives / E P I R A
rows.abstract:
... Upholding the rights and interests
of 118 electric cooperatives and their eight million consumers, Rep. Ping-ay informed his colleagues how Sec.60 of the Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA) which seeks to lower power rates through the condonation of the cooperatives´ P18-billion debt to the NEA, was incorrectly and improperly implemented resulting to NEA´s overcollection of said amount; cited several Executive Orders issued by the previous Administration to illustrate the resistance of a government bureaucracy to reform and its deliberate act to sabotage the will of Congress; called on the House to direct the Cttes. on Cooperatives Development and Energy to investigate, ... on the allegations of the overpayment to NEA of the amortization on the interest and principal of loans which were already condoned under EPIRA, the possibility of double payments made by the electric cooperatives and the PSALM Corporation,
and the necessity of refunding the amount of
overpayment back to the consumers; maintained that NEA and PSALM should correctly apply the provisions of the EPIRA which were intended to benefit the cooperatives and empower the consumers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT since 2010-11-09
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Paez. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.title_full: HIS REASONS FOR CHOOSING TO ALLY WITH THE OPPOSITION IN THE HOUSE
rows.title_short: On His Being In The Opposition
rows.abstract: ROSE TO EXPLAIN WHY HE CHOSE TO REMAIN IN THE OPPOSITION WHEN THE WISER CHOICE WAS TO JOIN THE ALLIES OF THE ADMINISTRATION.  STRESSED THAT HE HAD NEVER BEEN SWIFTY AND LOOSE IN CHANGING HIS POLITICAL AFFILIATION AS LONG AS HE BELIEVED IN HIS PARTY'S PROGRAM OF GOVERNMENT AND PERFORMANCE RECORD OF HIS PARTY'S LEADERS. mAINTAINED THAT HE DID NOT INTEND TO BE AN OBSTRUCTIONIST AND STAND AGAINST ANY POLICY OR PROGRAM INITIATIVE OF THE CURRENT GOVERNMENT. CALLED FOR A CRITICAL PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN THE MAJORITY AND MINORITY COALITIONS IN THE HOUSE AND ASKED THAT THEY LOOK AT EACH OTHER IN GOOD FAITH AND FIND NEW WAYS OF DELIVERING TO THE PEOPLE THE KIND OF GOVERNMENT THEY DESERVE. EXPRESSED HOPE THAT THE MEMBERS FIND COURAGE AND WISDOM TO WORK TOGETHER IN THE CHAMBER, NOT AS MEMBERS OF THE MAJORITY OR THE MINORITY, OR ALLIES OF
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2010-09-20

rows.title_full: HIS SENTIMENTS FOR CHOOSING TO ALLY WITH THE OPPOSITION IN THE HOUSE
rows.abstract: Rep. Marc Douglas C. Cagas IV said that during the September 15, 2010 meeting of the Mindanao Legislators with Speaker Feliciano Belmonte Jr., . . . it would have been best if the Speaker have spent more time to listen to their different concerns.
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2010-09-28

rows.author: G003
rows.abstract:
Rep. Aglipay spoke about the ff. issues, among others: 1) labor contractualization and how it is practiced through job contracting, fixed-term employment and probationary employment; 2) how many establishments circumvent the law to disregard the workers´ security of tenure and to avoid giving contractual workers the benefits which are usually given to regular workers; and 3) the positive effects of a guaranteed security of tenure on workers´ welfare in particular, and on economic development, in general. Urged the Body to revise and strengthen the provisions
of the Labor Code regarding security of tenure
and to encourage all affected sectors to work together to address the problem of labor contractualization.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2010-09-29)

rows.author: F048
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ong spoke on the unfair distribution of the
proposed national budget for fiscal year 2011 primarily the Dept. of Agriculture´s (DA) proposed budget of P37 billion only and the transfer of the NFA budget of P8 billion to the DSWD. He appealed to his colleagues to make the necessary corrective measures and to increase the budget allocation for DA so it can provide the necessary financial assistance to the deprived farmers and fisherfolks. He also asked the DBM to restore the P8 million budget of the NFA so the agency can effectively perform its mandate of ensuring rice subsidy and price stabilization. Finally, Rep. Ong appealed that Congress assert its power of the purse, and sought for the restoration of the requested P50 billion budget of the DA for 2011.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2010-09-29)
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Mariano, Escudero, Apostol, Paez and Rodriguez R. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F099
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ping-ay discussed the negative impact on
the tobacco industry of the DOH issuance of 1.) an Admin. Order imposing graphic warnings on cigarette packaging, and 2.) a joint memo circular issued by the DOH with the CSC prohibiting all gov't officials from interacting with members of the tobacco industry. He questioned the zeal with which the DOH contravenes the law in the guise of promoting public health, even as RA No. 9211 sought to institute the balanced policy towards
tobacco products and public health.
He revealed that the Philippines will be a signatory to a treaty that will be signed in Uruguay during the Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC) sponsored by the WHO
to be held in November 2010. He explained that the convention aims to regulate and reduce tobacco use that will in turn wipe out the entire tobacco industry and result in the loss of income and livelihood for millions of Filipinos. Finally, He urged the House to act on certain matters... and concluded that the tobacco industry is willing to work with the government in coming out with reasonable laws to regulate its activities.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2010-09-29)

rows.author: E047
rows.title_full: AGRARIAN REFORM ISSUE IN HACIENDA LUISITA
rows.abstract:
Saluted the farmers who died in the Hacienda Luisita massacre on November 16, 2004 and their leaders and supporters who became victims of extrajudicial killing. Decried the Cojuangco family´s economic and political maneuvers
to thwart the farmers´ fight for land reform such
as a referendum on the stock distribution option, a sugar plantation venture with a Chinese beverage maker, and the militarization of the hacienda under the guise of Philippine-American joint military exercises and civil-military and humanitarian missions. Pointed out that the President was a member of said
family, he urged the government to distribute the hacienda to the tillers thereof.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRARIAN REFORM since 2010-11-23

rows.author: A010
rows.title_full: ADVERSE EFFECTS OF THE AUGUST 23, 2010 HOSTAGE-TAKING ON THE TOURISM INDUSTRY IN THE COUNTRY
rows.title_short: Damages Of August 23, 2010, Hostage-taking Incident To The Tourism Industry
rows.abstract:
Stressed the negative effects of the August 23, 2010 hostagetaking incident in Luneta Park on tourism and investment travel and cited pertinent statistics. Asked the House to review budgetary support for tourist promotion. Urged the Members to immediately approve the Philippine Transportation Security Authority
Act in order to protect transport systems,
comply with the requirements of international conventions, and make transportation security a specialized service and function.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TOURISM since 2010-11-23

rows.title_full: \"GREEN EDSA\"
rows.abstract: Focused his speech on the alarming pollution levels in Metro Manila, particularly in the whole stretch of EDSA. Described how certain laws such as the Clean Air Act and the Biofuels Act had failed to abate air pollution coming from motor vehicles and then recommended the following: 1) for the DENR to declare Metro Manila, notably EDSA, as a “non-attainment area where specific pollutants have already exceeded ambient standards”; 2) to promote the expanded use of “green” or environment friendly PUVs; 3) for Congress to approve pending measures calling for the granting of incentives to the importation, manufacture, development, sale and distribution of environment-friendly vehicles; 4) the revision of the Clean Air Act to provide for stiffer fines and penalties for air polluters; and 5) to provide the State with emergency powers to revoke the franchises of PUVs who violate anti-pollution laws. Enjoined the Members to transform EDSA from a highway of death to the country´s first “green” highway.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2010-11-23

rows.author: G077
rows.title_full: DELAYS IN THE PAYMENT OF RETIRED GSIS MEMBERS
rows.title_short: Government Service Insurance System ( G S I S ) Assistance Upgrade
rows.abstract:
Brought to the attention of the Body the issue of human rights violations of the GSIS, particularly to its pensioners. Quoted from the letter-complaints of certain government retirees and pointed out that the snailpaced processing of GSIS pensions and claims had been a persistent and widespread problem involving
thousands of government retirees and pensioners all over the country. Urged the government
to institute the needed reforms that would provide a better pension and social security plan for the country´s senior citizens, whether GSIS retirees or not.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2010-11-23

rows.author: G009
rows.title_full: PLAGIARISM ISSUES IN THE SUPREME COURT
rows.title_short: Supreme Court's Decision To Absolve Justice Del Castillo In Plagiarism Case
rows.abstract:
Spoke about the Supreme Court ruling on the case of Vinuya vs. Executive Secretary penned by Justice Mariano del Castillo, denying the
petitions filed by rape survivors during World War II to force the Philippine government to seek redress from Japan on their behalf. Further related 1) how the counsels of the comfort women found that portions of the Vinuya decision were plagiarized for which reason they filed a supplemental motion for reconsideration; 2) why the Supreme Court dismissed the plagiarism case filed against Justice del Castillo and ordered the faculty members of the University of the Philippines (UP) College of Law to
show cause why they should not be held in contempt for issuing a statement about the alleged act of plagiarism and for asking Justice del Castillo to resign; and 3) how the High Court had made dishonesty a public policy and easy for anyone to commit intellectual theft.
Then asked the Supreme Court to review the
Vinuya case and also urged the Aquino government
to demand apology and remuneration from the
Japanese government on behalf of the Filipino comfort women.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2010-11-23
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Justice.

rows.author: F102
rows.title_full: DEPORTATION OF FILIPINO ACTIVIST IN SOUTH KOREA
rows.title_short: Deportation Of Filipinos From South Korea
rows.abstract:
Commended Pres. Benigno Simeon C. Aquino III for defending the Philippines during an international forum in Japan against allegations that the country was a terrorists´ haven. Criticized the DFA for its handling of the recent deportation of eight Filipinos in South Korea. Enjoined his colleagues to support the following initiatives to elicit the appropriate
apology and actions from the South Korean
government: for the DFA to lodge a diplomatic
protest against the South Korean government and to expel a number of South Korean diplomats and not allow their return or replacement until their government issues an apology and make reparations for its high-handed and arbitrary acts against the eight Filipinos. Proposed a calibrated retaliation for fear of the safety of OFWs in South Korea. Urged government officials to take their cue from Pres. Aquino´s response in Japan against the allegations of developed countries and to stand up to the Koreans´
alleged bullying so that South Korea would have
more respect for the Filipino people.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOREIGN AFFAIRS since 2010-11-23

rows.author: G102
rows.title_full: PASSAGE OF LAWS TO ELIMINATE VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN
rows.abstract: Dealt with the issue of women trafficking confronting many governments worldwide and informed the Body about her participation in the recent Regional Ministers´ and Parliamentarians´ Workshop on Review of Parliamentarians´ Actions and Legislations on the Elimination of Violence against Women held in Indonesia. Emphasized the need to ensure the effective implementation of laws addressing human trafficking and violence against women due to rising incidence of violence against women and the need to inform the public about women´s issues. Asked for the support of the Members in immediately enacting into law several measures which she had filed to address discrimination against women on account of sex, human trafficking, and prostitution.

rows.author: G001
rows.title_full: PROPER REPRESENTATION OF THE PHILIPPINES IN MAJOR INTERNATIONAL FISHERIES ORGANIZATIONS
rows.abstract:
Dwelt on the vital implications of the forthcoming annual session of the Western and
Central Pacific Fisheries Commission (WCPFC) particularly on the sustainability of the fishing industry in Mindanao in the light of the organization´s ban against tuna fishing. Underscored the importance of high-level representation in said convention of government officials such as the Secretaries of Agriculture
and Foreign Affairs, together with the director
of the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources,
to help promote and protect the interests of the local fisheries sector. Emphasized the need to create a sole government agency that will protect the Filipino fisherfolks and represent the interests of said sector in international conventions. Stated that changes should be initiated to sustain the productivity
of the country´s economy in general and of
the fisheries sector in particular.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AQUACULTURE AND FISHERIES RESOURCES since 2010-11-23

rows.author: G101
rows.abstract:
Commended and congratulated Rep. Pacquiao for bringing pride to the nation once again after securing his eighth world boxing title. Talked about the inspiring story of Rep.Pacquiao in both fields of sports and politics. Asked his peers to review the allocation for sports in
the 2011 National Budget Bill and to increase the
same, if necessary, for the sake of Filipino athletes.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2010-11-15)

rows.author: G063
rows.title_short: Pacquiao Re: Honor Of Being A Legislator And An Exceptional World Boxing Champ
rows.abstract:
Expressed his gratitude to the Filipino people for their prayers, cheers and support for him during his recent fight in the U.S. against Antonio Margarito of Mexico. Humbled and
honored by the Congressional Medal of Distinction
bestowed upon him by his colleagues that day, he
pointed out that his championship belts from eight different weight divisions not only belonged to him but also to the entire Filipino people who had shown the world that a Filipino can excel in a world-class arena through hard work, dedication and faith in God. Thanked Pres. Benigno Simeon C. Aquino III for his promise to help build the first public hospital in the province of Sarangani. Said that his eight championship belts were a first in the history of boxing and shall forever be known as the “Eighth Wonder of the World.”
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2010-11-22)

rows.author: G099
rows.title_full: EQUALITY OF WOMEN AND MEN UNDER THE LAW
rows.abstract:
Talked about the issues of gender equality and women empowerment in the Philippines. Lamented that gender inequality was evident in several

rows.author: F099
rows.title_full: COOPERATIVES' ROLE IN THE RECOVERY OF TYPHOON-AFFECTED AREAS IN NORTHERN LUZON
rows.title_short: Damage Caused By Typhoon Juan In Isabela
rows.abstract:
Focused on the plight of electric cooperatives in Northern Luzon whose operations were destroyed by typhoon Juan the previous
month, specifically the case of the Isabela Electric
Cooperative (ISELCO II). In this regard, he appealed
to the President for the immediate release of the necessary
calamity funds to help restore power in the
province of Isabela as well as to make them available
for financially distressed credit and multipurpose cooperatives
in the area.
(At this juncture, Deputy Speaker Remulla relinquished
the Chair to Rep. Rodolfo C. Fariñas.)
Moreover, Rep. Ping-ay suggested that the President
1) consider writing off crop loans for affected
farmers subsisting with the support of government financial
intermediaries; 2) provide additional calamity
assistance through the Conditional Cash Transfer Program;
and 3) use his discretionary funds to establish a
rescue fund through the Land Bank of the Philippines
for electric cooperatives which are genuinely owned
by their consumers as evidenced by their registration
with the Cooperative Development Authority.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT since 2010-11-30

rows.author: G067
rows.title_full: SENSELESS KILLING OF BOTANIST DR. LEONARDO CO
rows.abstract:
Took the floor to express sadness for the loss of Dr. Leonardo L. Co, a top plant taxonomist
and ethnobotanist who had served as museum
researcher in the University of the Philippines´
Institute of Biology and president of the Philippine Native Plants Conservation Society. Stressed how Dr. Co had touched the lives of the underprivileged members of society by citing his career accomplishments. Described the circumstances surrounding the death of Dr. Co and his team members while on an exploratory study in Kananga, Leyte under the auspices of the Energy Development Corp. Informed the Body that his Party-List Agham had filed a resolution calling for an immediate investigation and resolution of Dr. Co´s case.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2010-11-30

rows.author: F093
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR THE ELIMINATION OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN
rows.abstract:
Spoke on the rising incidence of violence against
women, the pervasiveness of sexual abuse and the responsibility that the government must assume to address such problems. Stressed the urgent need for Congress to amend existing laws, review the country´s compliance with the Convention to End all forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW) and implement measures to eradicate poverty that increases women and children´s vulnerability to violence. Challenged the government to manifest its stand on the United Nation´s (UN) decision regarding the case of Ms. Karen Vertido to ensure that women will no longer fall prey to all forms of violence and abuse.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2010-11-30

rows.author: G042
rows.title_full: ADVERSE EFFECT OF THE NUMBER OF CODING SCHEME BEING ENFORCED BY THE METRO MANILA DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (MMDA)ON PROVINCIAL BUSES
rows.abstract:
Delved on the “anti-poor and antipromdi”
number-coding scheme of the Metro Manila
Development Authority (MMDA) which seeks to reduce the number of buses plying EDSA by banning a specific category of buses from entering the major Metro Manila highway based on the ending plate of the buses. Cited the percentages of provincial and Metro
Manila buses as well as private vehicles which occupy EDSA. Suggested that the MMDA, the Land
Transportation Office (LTO) and the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB)focus on ridding out colorum buses of said
route. Appealed to the Members to approve
a resolution seeking the exemption of provincial
buses from said number-coding scheme and
thereafter welcomed Members who wish to coauthor
said Resolution.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2010-11-30
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Escudero, Tinga and Farinas.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F104
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR THE INCREASE IN THE BUDGET ALLOCATION OF STATE UNIVERSITIES AND COLLEGES (SUCS)
rows.abstract:
Talked about the just demand of State universities for a higher share in the country´s
budget, the problems plaguing the country´s education system, and why the government needed to rethink its education policies. Shared the concern of students who were convincing the Senate to make significant amendments in the 2011 General Appropriations Bill particularly to restore the slashed Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE)funding of State universities and provide some capital outlay to deserving schools. Indicated that students worldwide had been publicly demonstrating their principled stand against how governments had been treating education as a private commodity. Described how neoliberal globalization had caused the problems besetting the education sector and urged the Members to support the mass actions which the education community was scheduled to hold the following day.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2010-12-07
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Padilla, Gunigundo, Garin (J.), and Fua. Manifestation by Rep. Escudero. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: E059
rows.title_full: HUMAN TRAFFICKING CASES INVOLVING FILIPINOS IN THE UNITED STATES
rows.abstract:
Spoke on the issue of human trafficking and relayed to the Body the story and ordeal of 11 Filipinos who were deceived into working for a
cleaning company in the United States but who later turned out to be victims of illegal recruiters. Stressed that trafficking and slavery of migrant workers continue to happen to date and that the law should be enforced to its full extent for the protection of the rights and welfare of OFWs. Added that the country should comply with its own standards with regard to its workers and that every Filipino should follow the norms of justice of living honorably, not injuring others and rendering to every man his due.
rows.status: Scheduled for first meeting/hearing on 2011-05-25
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Bello and Sarmiento (M.) Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: A076
rows.title_full: FRAUDULENT USE OF HIS MEDICAL ASSISTANCE FUND IN GOVERNMENT HOSPITALS BY UNSCRUPULOUS PERSONS
rows.abstract: Raised concern re: congressional funds allocated by Members to different hospitals in the NCR for the benefit of their constituents whose illnesses could not be attended to by their local hospitals. Cited that his attention was called by the Philippine Heart Center administrator re: the faking of his signature by some unscrupulous people with dubious interest. Suggested that the Members coordinate with the hospital administrators regarding the manner by which their congressional funds were being dispensed. Asked the leadership of the House to protect the interest of their colleagues whose sole intention is to help their sick  constituents.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2010-12-07

rows.author: E041
rows.abstract:
Delved on the tension concerning the issue of housing for informal settlers which she rued must have stemmed from the government´s inability to respond to the mandate of the International Covenant on Economic, Social
and Cultural Rights and the provisions of the Urban Development and Housing Act (UDHA), particularly on the matter of relocation sites. Stressed that the government should issue an Executive Order allowing a moratorium on the demolition and a 5% allocation of the IRA of the cities and municipalities for housing
projects of informal settlers. Enjoined her
colleagues to support said allotment to address the housing problem in the country.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2010-12-06)

rows.author: G088
rows.abstract:
Reflected on the philosophy of law to clarify certain issues like the tasks of a legislator
and the laws of the land in relation to the natural moral law, which he opined is higher than the norms of the legal system. Stressed that the law must conform with morality, and asked how a law that promotes contraceptive sex, which is immoral, can be a valid law. Emphasized
that sex was intended by nature for procreation
that includes responsible parenthood to make the institution of marriage meaningful, and that to justify contraceptive sex would be to justify divorce as there would be no need for permanence in the partnership of the spouses. Discussed about contraception, sex during the infertile periods, abstention or the nonuse of sex during fertile periods; and the State authority over population control programs.  Expressed belief that society should leave the proper regulation of the propagation of offspring to the married couples´ principle of subsidiarity, without the undue influence of propaganda and other inducements or coercive measures, whether State-sponsored, foreign funded or financed by big business, and certainly without “legitimizing” immoral acts through legislation. Reps. Apostol and Socrates discussed the the ill-effects of abortion drugs known as RU-486 and quinacrine hydrocholoride; the huge budget allocation by the DOH for the purchase of contraceptives; the country´s population growth; financing of the RH Bill by World Bank and US billionaires.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2010-12-06)
rows.remarks: Interpellation and manifestation by Rep. Apostol; Manifestations by Reps. Golez (R.)and Gonzales (N.) Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G118
rows.abstract:
Dwelt on the plight of Philippine coconut
farmers who have been suffering due to the
dismal state of the coconut industry; the problems besieging said industry which not only drag the industry down the drain but the overall economic performance of the Philippines as well; and the dismal allocation of funds for the Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) during the past years. Asked the Department of Agriculture for more policy interventions on the coconut industry and expressed hope it would be given priority.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. FUA
On Rep. Fua´s queries, Rep. Garin (S.) replied
that the Members should not ignore the issue on coconut levy funds and pointed out that the outdated law on cutting of coconut trees should be revisited and revised, and that the PCA Charter should be updated. Added that the Body can come up with legislations to defend and support the coconut industry.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2010-12-06)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Fua. Referred to the appropriate committee.
